jobs.referencePlan: Two ordered original references: first is the exact grounded conventional floor geometry; second is gray anatomical appearance only. Preserve reference 1 pose, perspective and movement headroom.
jobs.promptText:
RESTYLE IMAGE 1 WITHOUT CHANGING ITS GROUNDED DEADLIFT SETUP. The FIRST supplied image is the authoritative POSE, BARBELL, FLOOR-CONTACT, CAMERA and FRAMING reference. The SECOND image supplies only the gray striated anatomical APPEARANCE. When references differ, IMAGE 1 ALWAYS WINS for position and equipment geometry. No written content, colored patch, dots, arrows or overlays.

PRESERVE IMAGE 1'S EXACT STARTING GEOMETRY. Keep both existing plate bottom rims resting on the same floor plane in their original positions, with the same contact shadows and no gap beneath them. Keep the bar shaft at its original fixed floor-start height through the plate centers. Keep the same feet, shoe-floor contacts, hand grips, straight arm reach, hip hinge, knee bend and long inclined trunk. The mannequin remains bent to the grounded bar BEFORE the lift. Do not raise the bar or either plate toward a standing body. Do not straighten the torso or arms upward to resemble IMAGE 2. Do not create a hanging bar at the knees, smaller plates, blocks, floating equipment or new support surfaces.

USE IMAGE 2 FOR GRAYSCALE ANATOMICAL MATERIAL ONLY. Replace the smooth ivory appearance with the same original gray/silver athletic anatomical mannequin and clearly differentiated superficial muscle contours, crisp grooves and fine readable muscle-fiber striations. Retain IMAGE 1's skeleton/joint positions and realistic proportions while changing only the visible surface treatment. Remove IMAGE 1's navy sleeveless top so the torso and arms have exposed neutral gray anatomical surfaces. Use opaque dark gray fitted TRAINING SHORTS and actual closed gray low-profile TRAINING SHOES, keeping IMAGE 1's foot positions and shoe-floor contacts. Keep the barbell and plates gray. Do not copy IMAGE 2's orange shoulders, dumbbells, standing pose or landscape crop. Every exposed body surface stays gray; no orange or other colored region appears. Clean non-gory material, neutral face, short neutral hair, no exposed organs or wounds.

KEEP IMAGE 1'S PORTRAIT CAMERA AND MOVEMENT SPACE. Preserve the complete grounded barbell, shoes, knees, hands and their spatial relations. Retain the substantial empty headroom above the crouched mannequin for the SAME adult to stand fully upright later without a camera move. Do not shrink that headroom by enlarging or straightening the starting person. Preserve the actual perspective floor plane while changing its surface and the studio background to plain white with soft diffuse lighting and grounded shadows. Include no rack, bench, extra weights or decorative equipment.

This is one normal conventional floor-deadlift starting still. Both hands grip the same grounded shaft just outside the legs; bar stays over midfoot and close to the shins, arms straight, hips above knees, trunk long and braced. The entire purpose of the first reference is to retain its established floor contact and reachable bar geometry. Show only one figure and one barbell. No labels, words, numbers, titles, captions, logos, muscle markers or line graphics.

jobs.name: Barbell Deadlift
jobs.title: Anatomical 3D · Movement
jobs.alt: Barbell Deadlift: One conventional floor deadlift from the gripped floor setup to standing and a real controlled lowering to the floor.
jobs.teachingCoverage: One conventional floor deadlift from the gripped floor setup to standing and a real controlled lowering to the floor.
canonicalInstructions: Stand with the bar over the middle of the feet.
Hinge and bend the knees to grip it, brace the trunk, then stand with the bar close to the legs; reverse the movement to lower.
jobs.anatomicalAccentPolicy: NO ORANGE ACCENT IN THIS EXERCISE. The catalog primary group is the glutes, which are covered by the required dark gray shorts. Keep all exposed skin and equipment gray, keep shorts opaque dark gray, and do not color the shorts or substitute hamstrings/lower back as the primary. Accompanying Form text will identify the primary group; visual accuracy takes priority over always showing an orange area.
